title: Update from Hell: Can Coding Agents Survive Hidden Breakage in Dependency Upgrades?
abstract: arXiv:2608.30300v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Modern software systems rely heavily on third-party dependencies, but upgrading those dependencies remains a costly maintenance activity. Dependency upgrades do not always preserve the function signatures, type systems, APIs, or runtime semantics assumed by existing code. Consequently, developers often need to perform source code adaptations to accommodate dependency-induced changes. However, such code-level changes are often not explicitly communicated to project maintainers, posing a significant challenge to software reliability.   Meanwhile, coding agents have emerged as a new form of software development tool and are increasingly adopted by developers due to their automation capabilities. In this paper, we introduce DEPBENCH, a benchmark consisting of 203 real-world dependency-upgrade tasks across five package ecosystems spanning five language communities, each involving hidden code-level changes that require source code adaptation.

translated_title: 来自地狱的更新：编码智能体能否在依赖升级的隐性破坏中存活下来？
translated_abstract: 现代软件系统严重依赖第三方依赖项，但升级这些依赖项仍然是一项成本高昂的维护活动。依赖升级并不总是能保留现有代码所依赖的函数签名、类型系统、API 或运行时语义。因此，开发人员通常需要执行源代码适配来应对依赖项引发的变化。然而，此类代码级别的更改往往不会明确传达给项目维护人员，这对软件可靠性构成了重大挑战。与此同时，编码智能体作为一种新型软件开发工具出现，并因其自动化能力而被开发人员日益广泛地采用。在本文中，我们介绍了 DEPBENCH，这是一个由 203 个真实世界依赖升级任务组成的基准测试，涵盖五个语言社区的五个包生态系统，每个任务都涉及需要源代码适配的隐藏代码级更改。
tldr: 该论文提出了 DEPBENCH 基准，包含跨越五个语言社区五个包生态系统的 203 个真实依赖升级任务，用于评估编码智能体能否应对依赖升级中隐藏的代码级破坏并完成源代码适配。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces DEPBENCH, a benchmark of 203 real-world dependency-upgrade tasks across five package ecosystems and five language communities, designed to evaluate whether coding agents can survive hidden code-level breakage in dependency upgrades.
